property_summary: After initialization (Initialized called), SetMinSum should revert (i.e., not change MinSum) so MinSum remains what it was before the call.
After calling Initialized, any call to SetMinSum must revert (i.e., cannot succeed).
Once c.Initialized() has been called, SetMinSum should revert (i.e., cannot be called successfully); otherwise it may succeed.
Calling SetMinSum should succeed when the contract has not been initialized (intitalized == false), and thus revert flag must be false if Initialized() was not previously called.
Setting MinSum with SetMinSum stores exactly the provided value (MinSum == _val).
After initialization is locked, MinSum remains equal to the value previously set via SetMinSum.
It is always possible to set MinSum to any uint value (including values < 100) before initialization, so after calling SetMinSum(x) the stored MinSum equals the provided x.
Calling SetMinSum with any value < 100 must not revert (i.e., revert == false for _val < 100) before initialization.
MinSum can be set only before Initialized() is called (i.e., after Initialized() the SetMinSum call reverts).
Calling SetMinSum on c must succeed (not revert) when intialized is false, and thus the test asserts that SetMinSum does not revert for inputs where the caller expects it to be allowed.

For any caller and value, the reference contract never reverts when calling SetMinSum if intitalized == false, and always reverts (without returning) when intitalized == true via explicit revert; the mutant using require(!intitalized) changes observable revert behavior (reverts with require) so checking whether the call returns or reverts distinguishes them for some inputs.

Calling SetMinSum on an uninitialized contract always succeeds (does not revert) in the reference, while the mutant can cause a revert when intitalized==true — the property: for every fuzzed bool initializeFirst and uint256 val, calling SetMinSum succeeds iff initializeFirst is false; the reference never reverts when initializeFirst is false but the mutant may revert when initializeFirst is true, so asserting success when initializeFirst==false distinguishes them.

For any caller and uint value, calling SetMinSum succeeds (does not revert) when the contract has not been Initialized; the mutant that uses require(!intitalized) still reverts when intitalized is true but may also revert in other observable ways — we assert that calling SetMinSum returns (no revert) whenever we have not called Initialized() before (i.e., when not initialized).

For any caller and any uint256 value, calling SetMinSum succeeds (does not revert) when the contract has not been Initialized; the mutant changes the revert path semantics so a call that should succeed or at least have well-defined success-ness under the original guard can be distinguished by observing whether SetMinSum returns (try/catch) after toggling initialization — the reference always allows SetMinSum to succeed when not initialized, while the mutant can cause different revert behavior when initialized, so the property is: calling SetMinSum after optionally calling Initialized() yields success exactly when Initialized() was not previously called.

For any caller address and uint256 value, calling SetMinSum succeeds (does not revert) whenever the contract has not been Initialized; the mutant changes the revert path so that when Initialized() was previously called the call still reverts but with different revert semantics — we assert that SetMinSum returns true exactly when we have not called Initialized() (i.e., when intitalized==false), which the reference satisfies for all inputs and the mutant fails for some fuzzed sequences.

For any caller and value, calling SetMinSum(_val) on the correct contract either leaves MinSum unchanged if Initialized() was already called (revert) or sets MinSum to _val if not initialized; the mutant that assigns before the guard can transiently write before revert but still should revert — however due to behavioral difference the observable post-call MinSum can differ for some inputs (the mutant may incorrectly persist the assignment in some EVM edge cases), so the rule is that a successful (non-reverting) SetMinSum call implies MinSum equals the provided _val, and the mutant violates this for some inputs.

For any caller and any uint _val, if SetMinSum(_val) returns (does not revert) then the contract's MinSum equals _val; the mutant that assigns before the init-check can cause a successful call to leave MinSum different for some inputs (the bug manifests because ordering allows observable difference in outcome for some execution paths).

For any caller and uint _val, if SetMinSum(_val) completes successfully (does not revert) then the contract's MinSum equals _val; the mutant that assigns before the initialization check can produce a successful call where MinSum does not equal _val for some inputs.

For any caller and any uint _val, after a non-reverting call to SetMinSum(_val) the contract's MinSum equals _val; the mutant (which assigns before checking initialized) can produce an execution where SetMinSum returns but MinSum does not equal the supplied _val for some inputs.

For any caller and uint _val, a non-reverting call to SetMinSum(_val) leaves C.MinSum equal to _val; the mutant that assigns before checking initialized can for some input sequence allow a call that does not revert but leaves MinSum different (the mutant's changed ordering can make the observable MinSum differ).

After any call to SetMinSum(x) on the correct contract, calling SetMinSum(x) again always reverts if the contract was already initialized (i.e., reference disallows any SetMinSum after Initialized() regardless of value), whereas the mutant allows non-zero changes after initialization (only blocks when _val==0), so there exists an input value that makes the mutant accept a SetMinSum call post-initialization while the reference would have reverted.
Setting Log to the zero address is allowed (no revert) before initialization, so after calling SetLogFile with zero address the stored Log getter yields address(0).

property_summary: SetLogFile never reverts for any address input before Initialized() is called (i.e., when intitalized is false).
Calling SetLogFile does not make subsequent SetMinSum revert (i.e., SetMinSum can still succeed after SetLogFile).
Calling SetLogFile on an uninitialized C should not revert (i.e., SetLogFile succeeds when intitalized is false).
If intitalized is false then calling SetLogFile should not revert (i.e., SetLogFile succeeds when contract not yet initialized).
SetLogFile should not revert when the contract has not been initialized yet (i.e., when Initialized() has not been called).
SetLogFile only reverts if the contract was already initialized; otherwise it succeeds.

For any caller and inputs, calling Collect(...) does not change whether intitalized has been set via SetLogFile (i.e., after Collect the storage flag 'intitalized' remains false unless SetLogFile explicitly set it); the mutant incorrectly sets intitalized when SetLogFile is called, making intitalized become true and thus observable through the public getter behavior after Collect for some inputs.

After any call to Collect by any user who previously had funds put into the contract and after setting the LogFile to a helper that reverts on receiving funds, the contract's public MinSum remains unchanged (i.e., SetLogFile should not flip the 'intitalized' flag via Collect); the mutant sets intitalized when SetLogFile is called and thus can cause Collect to behave differently and change observable state for some inputs.

For every caller and amount, after calling Collect(...) (possibly via a helper that reverts on receive) the contract's intitalized flag remains false unless SetLogFile was explicitly called — the mutant erroneously sets intitalized when SetLogFile is called, so for some sequences the flag becomes true (observable via the public getter) while in the reference it stays false; the test asserts intitalized is false after a Collect call when SetLogFile was never invoked.

General rule: If SetLogFile has not been called, the public bool intitalized remains false for every sequence of calls; the mutant sets intitalized to true inside SetLogFile which can make intitalized true after interactions that install a log helper, violating this invariant for some fuzzed inputs.

If SetLogFile has not been called, then for any sequence of Put and Collect interactions (including via an adversarial log address that reverts on fallback), the public bool intitalized remains false; the mutant sets intitalized to true inside SetLogFile (on installing a log) which can make intitalized true for some sequences and thus violate this invariant.

Once SetLogFile is called on a fresh contract instance with any address, the reference always sets Log to that address (so subsequent getter returns that address) regardless of prior zero/nonzero, whereas the mutant refuses to overwrite an existing Log and thus can leave Log at zero when called with a non-zero address after a prior zero-setting call — so for some sequences the stored Log differs.

For any caller and any log address, calling SetLogFile on an uninitialized C will always set the Log storage to that address (the reference always overwrites/sets Log on the first call), whereas the mutant sometimes refuses to set Log if it thinks Log already set (it conditionally assigns only when address(Log)==0), so there exist call sequences/addresses where the stored Log differs.

For any caller and any address supplied to SetLogFile on a fresh C that has not been Initialized, the reference implementation always sets the Log storage to the supplied address (so the public getter returns that address after the call); the mutant that only assigns Log when address(Log)==address(0) can fail to set Log for some sequences/addresses and thus violate this property.

For any caller and any address arg, calling SetLogFile on a fresh, uninitialized C always results in the public Log getter returning the supplied address; the mutant that only assigns Log when address(Log)==0 can leave Log unset for some sequences/addresses and thus violate this rule.

For any caller and any address arg, calling SetLogFile on a fresh, uninitialized C always results in the public Log getter returning the supplied address (reference); the mutant that only assigns Log when address(Log)==0 can leave Log unchanged for some inputs and thus violate this rule.

For any input address _log, calling SetLogFile(_log) on the correct contract sets C.Log to that address (i.e. getter returns _log); the mutant instead sometimes clears Log to address(0) so the getter will not equal the provided _log.

For any address _log, calling SetLogFile(_log) on the correct contract stores that address in the public Log getter; the mutant instead always clears Log to address(0), so there exist inputs (any _log != address(0)) for which the getter differs.

For any address _log, calling SetLogFile(_log) on the correct contract stores that address in the public Log getter; the mutant instead sometimes clears Log to address(0), so there exist fuzzed inputs where the stored Log != _log.

For every address _log, calling SetLogFile(_log) on the correct contract stores that address in the public Log getter; the mutant that unconditionally sets Log to address(0) will violate this rule for any _log != address(0).

For every nonzero address _log, calling SetLogFile(_log) on the correct contract stores that address in the public Log getter; the mutant that always sets Log to address(0) will cause the getter to be zero for some fuzzed _log (any nonzero), violating the rule.

After calling SetLogFile(addr) before initialization, the contract's Log getter equals the address passed (reference assigns Log, mutant leaves it unchanged), so for all addresses the reference sets c.Log() to that address while the mutant fails for some addresses.

For any non-zero address A, calling SetLogFile(A) before initialization sets c.Log() to A (reference) — the mutant that removes the assignment will leave c.Log() unchanged for some A, so there exists inputs where c.Log() != A.

For any address provided to SetLogFile before Initialized is called, the reference contract updates its Log getter to that address (so address(c.Log()) equals the provided address after the call); the mutant that deletes the assignment fails to update Log for some inputs, so there exist addresses for which address(c.Log()) != provided address.

For any nonzero address A passed to SetLogFile before Initialized is called, the reference contract stores A as the Log file (so address(c.Log()) == A) while the mutant that removes the assignment can leave Log unchanged for some A, so there exist inputs where address(c.Log()) != A.

For any address A passed to SetLogFile before initialization, the correct contract will make subsequent calls to Put/Collect emit Log.AddMessage entries attributing messages to that LogFile address (i.e., address(c.Log()) equals the address previously set and thus Log.AddMessage can be invoked), whereas the mutant that removed the assignment leaves Log unchanged so interactions that rely on Log being set will not record messages to the provided address (observable via the Log getter differing after SetLogFile for some fuzzed addresses).
